text:
Education in Pakistan follows a national system largely inspired by the English educational system. The formal education structure begins with pre-school (for children aged 3–5), followed by junior school (years 1 to 5), and then middle school (years 6 to 8). The eight common disciplines studied in junior school include Arts, Computer Studies and ICT, General Science (covering Physics, Chemistry, and Biology), Modern languages and literature (Urdu and English), Mathematics, Religious Education (Islamic Studies), Social Studies, and Pakistan Studies.
Secondary education begins in year 9 and lasts four years, requiring students to pass national examinations administered by a regional Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (BISE) upon completion of year 10 (SSC/Matriculation). Students then attend intermediate college for years 11 and 12 to receive the Higher Secondary School Certificate (HSSC). Alternative qualifications include the General Certificate of Education (GCE) and International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE). The system faces significant challenges, notably a pervasive gender disparity, with low female enrollment and literacy rates compared to males. Furthermore, the quality of education is criticized for having an outdated curriculum, teacher shortages, and an over-reliance on rote learning.
